config.notes: The orchestrator (your main session) runs on this tier. claude-opus-4-8 is the stable safety-carrying tier that never trips the per-message cyber guard, so the orchestrator can read, summarize, and route security findings without disruptive mid-session model swaps; it costs less than the frontier tier and does not draw down a capped frontier allowance on high-volume routing traffic. Stored once so a single edit moves it. If moved to claude-fable-5: orchestration and peer-agent communication quality improves (the frontier tier's core strength), but every routing message touching coding or security content risks a per-message auto-swap to Opus, the frontier tier draws down its allowance faster and is subject to plan caps, and security-task routing text itself can trip the guard; in that configuration all security content must be kept strictly inside the 4.8-pinned subagents so the trigger's own messages stay clean.

task_tier_rules.rationale: Design and spec framing is where capability compounds; predictably code-heavy design should start on Opus 5 to avoid paying frontier drawdown for guard-swapped output.
Opus 5 matches the frontier tier closely on structured reasoning at half the cost and no allowance cap; escalate to Fable only when the problem is ambiguity-dominated.
Hard constraint: 4.8 is the stable tier that does not trip the per-message cyber guard; never execute security work on Fable or Opus 5.
With a full spec Sonnet delivers near-parity output at a fraction of the cost and parallelizes cleanly.
Roughly 3 or fewer tool calls with a specific question; any larger model is pure waste.
Sustained multi-subagent orchestration is a named frontier-tier strength that compounds over long sessions; keep security content out of its messages to avoid guard swaps.
Navigating ambiguity is the frontier tier's headline strength and this work is mostly prose, so it rarely trips the coding auto-swap; low volume keeps allowance impact small.
Documentation from existing source material is structured transformation Sonnet does well; escalate to Opus 5 only for architecture-narrative docs needing real synthesis.
Review compounds, but Fable auto-swaps to Opus on code content anyway, making Opus 5 the effective ceiling at lower cost; fast mode helps latency-sensitive gates.
Well-trodden patterns with clear acceptance criteria; Sonnet is the reliability floor (Haiku only for genuinely trivial single-file changes).

agent_defaults.rationale: Every task this agent runs is security work, so its default IS the security pin (claude-opus-4-8). Pin by full ID in the agent definition; do not rely on the opus alias, which can resolve to a guard-tripping tier.
Offensive-security engagement lead; permanently pinned to 4.8 including attack-narrative synthesis. Agent-definition full-ID surface only.
Pentest execution is guard-tripping content by definition; pinned to 4.8 via the agent-definition full-ID surface.
UI and component implementation against a spec is Sonnet's sweet spot; escalate gnarly state-management or accessibility-architecture problems to Opus.
API and service implementation given a spec fits Sonnet; escalate destructive schema/migration design decisions to Opus before execution.
Test authoring, coverage passes, and bug repro are mechanical and parallelizable; escalate flaky-test root-cause hunts to Opus.
Quality-gate verdicts compound; Opus 5 is the effective ceiling for code content anyway since Fable auto-swaps on it.
System design, ADRs, and trade-off framing are exactly where the frontier tier's ambiguity and spec-framing strength compounds; low task volume keeps drawdown acceptable.
Product and UX design - journeys, wireframes, interaction and visual design - is creative, ambiguity-heavy work where the frontier tier's strength compounds.

Requirements and epic breakdown from a stated goal is structured-reasoning prose work Sonnet handles reliably at a fraction of the cost; escalate genuinely ambiguous greenfield discovery to Fable, or to Opus 5 when a breakdown needs deep synthesis.
Docs and knowledge-base maintenance from existing material is structured transformation; Sonnet is the best token-to-quality tier for it.
Versioning, changelog collation, and release checklists are procedural but consequential; Sonnet is the reliability floor, Haiku acceptable for pure changelog collation sub-steps.
Lateral thinking and assumption-challenging is ambiguity work where the frontier tier is strongest; invitation-only usage keeps volume and allowance cost minimal.

notes: Model surfaces: a sub-agent definition's model: frontmatter accepts a full model ID; the live Agent tool takes only aliases {fable, opus, sonnet, haiku}. Aliases can move between model versions and are not guaranteed to resolve to a specific model, so never rely on an alias to reach a security-critical tier - pin claude-opus-4-8 by full ID in the definition and re-verify periodically.

Security enforcement is by ROUTING, not a per-agent override column. Hand security / dual-use / red-team / pentest / exploit / vuln / credential work to the security-tier agents (reviewer-security, testing-red-team, testing-pentester), which are pinned to claude-opus-4-8 via full-ID frontmatter. A plugin agent's model is fixed at definition time and cannot self-switch mid-task, so there is no enforceable per-agent override; the routing decision is the control.

Frontier-tier allowance discipline: the frontier tier (Fable) draws down its allowance faster than Opus and is subject to plan caps (exact rates are plan-specific). Reserve it for tiers where its ambiguity/design/orchestration strength compounds (design/spec, long orchestration, brainstorm, architect, designer, loki). Do not route mechanical or logic-bound work to it.

Frontier per-message auto-swap: any frontier-tier (Fable) message touching coding, cybersecurity, or biology auto-swaps to Opus per-message. Routing code-dense work through it often yields Opus output while consuming a frontier-shaped slot, so code-heavy tiers are assigned to Opus 5 or Sonnet directly.

trigger_model is stored once in config so the orchestrator tier is edited in one place; if later moved to claude-fable-5, keep all security execution inside 4.8-pinned subagents so the orchestrator's own guard-tripping message volume stays near zero.
Opus 5 fast mode is available (Opus 5 only) and fits latency-sensitive quality gates (code review) and high-throughput reasoning passes.

Destructive schema/migration changes: the backend developer (developer-backend) must escalate the design decision to a capable tier and follow backup-first, manual-SQL, data-loss-warning policy before execution, regardless of its Sonnet default.
Prefer the explicit full ID (claude-opus-4-8) in sub-agent definitions for stability; do not assume an alias resolves to a given version without checking.
